    Codon usage weights from a reference set of genes

    Source: R/bio-sequence.R
    bio_codon_weights.Rd

    Counts codons in a reference set of coding sequences (usually highly expressed genes) and returns relative synonymous codon usage (RSCU) and the relative adaptiveness w of each codon, as defined by Sharp and Li (1987). Codons that never occur in the reference get a count of 0.5, as in the original method. These weights drive bio_cai() and bio_codon_optimise().

    Usage

    bio_codon_weights(.data, seq = NULL, code = "standard")

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame, tibble or bio_seq_tbl().

    seq

    <tidy-select> The sequence column. Can be omitted for a <bio_seq_tbl>.

    code

    Genetic code used to group synonymous codons; see bio_translate().

    Value

    A tibble with one row per codon and columns codon, amino_acid, count, rscu and w.

    References

    Sharp, P. M. and Li, W.-H. (1987). The codon adaptation index: a measure of directional synonymous codon usage bias, and its potential applications. Nucleic Acids Research, 15, 1281-1295. doi:10.1093/nar/15.3.1281

    Examples

    ecoli_cds |>
  dplyr::filter(class == "ribosomal") |>
  bio_codon_weights(sequence) |>
  dplyr::filter(amino_acid == "L")
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   codon amino_acid count   rscu       w
#>   <chr> <chr>      <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 TTA   L             15 0.179  0.0356 
#> 2 TTG   L             21 0.25   0.0499 
#> 3 CTT   L             25 0.298  0.0594 
#> 4 CTC   L             20 0.238  0.0475 
#> 5 CTA   L              2 0.0238 0.00475
#> 6 CTG   L            421 5.01   1
